location: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, Key Largo (afternoon program locations to be confirmed)
summary: A one-day marine science program for 115 students, organized into four cohorts rotating through hands-on experiences led by REEF educators, from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

rotation.heading: Four Cohorts, One Coordinated Day
rotation.intro: Students will be divided into four cohorts of approximately 28–29 students. Cohorts rotate among the glass-bottom boat tour, citizen science and fish identification, the lionfish lesson, a scheduled lunch, and two afternoon programs on marine ecology and endangered species. Activities run concurrently, so the schedule below shows where each cohort will be throughout the day.

departure.label: Departure
departure.note: The program day ends at 5:00 PM. The final half hour is flexible time for wrap-up and departure.

notes: This is a planning schedule. Exact activity order, timing, and locations may be refined before the program, and REEF will confirm the final schedule with you.
Each activity is planned as a one-hour program; the time between activities allows for transitions.
Every cohort has the same one-hour lunch. Lunch periods are staggered so the picnic area is not crowded.
The glass-bottom boat tour times are set by the boat schedule. The other programs are arranged around them.
Your group arrives on three buses, and the program begins at 9:00 AM.

days.title: One Day on the Reef
days.theme: Four cohorts rotate through five hands-on experiences led by REEF educators, from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

blocks.title: Glass-Bottom Boat Tour
blocks.description: Students view living coral reef habitat and the fish that depend on it from a glass-bottom boat, with a REEF educator helping them connect what they see to how healthy reefs work.

blocks.title: Citizen Science & Fish Identification
blocks.description: Students learn how REEF's volunteer divers and snorkelers identify fish and record what they see, then practice the same identification and survey skills used in REEF's Volunteer Fish Survey Project.

blocks.title: Lionfish Lesson & Dissection
blocks.description: Students investigate invasive lionfish through a guided dissection, looking at anatomy and adaptations and learning why lionfish are a conservation challenge for Florida Keys reefs.

blocks.title: Picnic Lunch
blocks.description: Each cohort has the same one-hour picnic lunch. Lunch is not provided, so students and chaperones should bring a packed lunch.

blocks.title: Marine Ecology
blocks.description: A REEF educator-led program on how reef, seagrass, and mangrove communities work and how the species within them depend on one another. Two cohorts join each one-hour session.

blocks.title: Endangered Species
blocks.description: A REEF educator-led program on threatened and endangered species of the Florida Keys, why they are at risk, and what people can do to help protect them. Two cohorts join each one-hour session.

studentsWill: Observe living coral reef habitat and marine life from the glass-bottom boat.
Learn and practice the fish identification and survey methods REEF's citizen scientists use.
Investigate invasive lionfish anatomy and adaptations through a guided dissection.
Explore how marine ecosystems function and why some Florida Keys species are endangered.
Connect what they see to REEF's ongoing reef conservation and invasive-species work.

logistics.transportation: Your school arranges transportation to and from the park. The group arrives on three buses, and park entrance fees for all three buses are included. Transportation between program locations is still being explored and is not part of this proposal.
logistics.familyTransportation: Students travel to and from the park by school bus. Your school will share departure and return times.
logistics.meals: Lunch is not provided. Students and chaperones bring a packed lunch, and each cohort has a scheduled picnic lunch at the park. REEF staff can recommend delivery options.
logistics.lunch: Packed lunches from home. Each cohort eats at its own scheduled time in the park picnic area, between 11:00 AM and 12:30 PM.
logistics.arrival: Buses arrive at John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park for a 9:00 AM start.
logistics.transitions: Short gaps between activities are transition time for moving between the marina, the picnic area and program areas. This is a planning schedule, so exact timing may be refined before the program.
logistics.departure: The program day ends at 5:00 PM. The final half hour is flexible time for wrap-up and departure.
